articles.title: CRM Search
articles.summary: Instant search over contacts, accounts, and orders from anywhere — Ctrl+K, type, done. Select rows to launch bulk actions and campaigns.

beginner.text: Press Ctrl+K on any CRM page. Type a name, email, or phone number and results appear immediately. A type filter narrows to Contacts or Accounts; clicking a result opens it.
Your last search is remembered, so reopening the modal picks up where you left off.

intermediate.text: Tick rows to build a selection — a summary bar appears with bulk actions: open every selected record in tabs, create a Quick Task, or Run Campaign to email all of them (see Bulk Email from a Selection).
Filter chips and saved quick presets sit above the results for one-click refinement.

advanced.text: The filter button opens the Query Builder for grouped AND/OR conditions with field-specific operators — see its dedicated article. Records you visit are also indexed locally, which is what makes repeat searches instant.

articles.title: Query Builder
articles.summary: Grouped AND/OR condition builder for CRM Search — build precise audience queries and save them for reuse.

advanced.text: Open it from the filter button inside CRM Search. Add conditions (field, operator, value) and group them with AND/OR logic — for example: state is TX AND (order count > 5 OR YTD > $2,000).
Apply runs the query immediately; Save stores it by name so you — or a campaign — can reuse the exact audience later.
Saved queries are the cleanest way to define campaign audiences: build once, verify the results visually, then select-all and Run Campaign.

articles.title: New Contact
articles.summary: Quick-create a CRM contact from anywhere with Ctrl+Q — search for the account, fill in the basics, done.

beginner.text: Press Ctrl+Q (or use the Actions Shelf). Search for and attach the account, then fill first name, last name, email, phone, and company. Create posts the contact straight to the CRM.
By default a contact must be attached to an account. Admins can relax this under Developer Settings → 'New Contact requires an account'.

articles.title: Quick Task
articles.summary: Create a CRM task in seconds: pick a template, set priority and a due date like +1w, submit.

beginner.text: From a contact, account, or order page, open Quick Task (Actions Shelf → Add Task, or popup → Tools). The filter bar is focused — type to find a task template, press Enter, adjust, submit. The task attaches to the contact in the CRM.

intermediate.text: Press '/' to enter composer mode and fill category, priority, subject, and description entirely from the keyboard, with a live preview alongside.
Save your recurring follow-ups as task templates (Template Editor → Task tab) — two keystrokes beats retyping the same task every day.

articles.title: Task List
articles.summary: Your CRM task list in a fast modal — search, filter by status and priority, sort, and act on many tasks at once.

beginner.text: Press Ctrl+X to see your tasks without navigating to the CRM task page. Search, filter by status or priority, and click a task to open its record.

intermediate.text: Tick rows for bulk actions: open all in tabs, create a follow-up Quick Task, or Run Campaign to email every selected task's contact with one template.
The list reflects your CRM tasks page — if a task doesn't appear, confirm it exists in the CRM and that it's assigned to you.

articles.title: Call Log
articles.summary: Keyboard-first call logging: filter to a template, '/' through category, direction, and notes, and submit to the CRM activity log.

beginner.text: On a contact or account page, open Log Call from the Actions Shelf. The modal shows the contact's name and phone; type to filter call templates or press '/' to compose from scratch.
Set the category, direction (inbound/outbound), and voicemail flag, write the note, and submit — the call lands in the CRM activity log immediately.

intermediate.text: The whole flow is keyboard-driven: '/' enters the composer, Enter advances fields, and the preview pane shows exactly what will be logged. With templates for your common call outcomes, logging takes under ten seconds.

articles.title: Phone Finder
articles.summary: Scans a contact's order history for phone numbers and saves your pick to the contact record.

beginner.text: Contact missing a phone number? Run Phone Finder from the contact page. It scans the contact's orders, collects every phone number found (each labeled with the shipping name it came from), and shows a picker. Choose one and it saves to the contact automatically.
